posts.title: LinkedIn: why AerSynk exists
alt: Why AerSynk exists: built by people who fly drones for a living. Diagram of photos, LiDAR, magnetics and spectral data flowing from four separate boxes into one workspace.
posts.linkedin:
Why AerSynk exists.

As a Drone Solutions Advisor, our founder Kwazi Khumalo helped clients find the right drone setup. One problem kept coming up: survey teams lose hours moving data between separate tools. Photos in one program, LiDAR in another, magnetic and spectral data in specialist software, and a GIS analyst lining it all up by hand.

AerSynk Survey is our answer: one workspace where every flight and every sensor sits on the same map, from planning to finished deliverable. Today it is a working prototype on demo data, and we are building real-data processing one sensor at a time.

Alongside the software, we fly. Kwazi is a BVLOS-certified remote pilot available for agriculture, mapping, security, inspection and filming work (flown under an approved partner operator's certificate), and we consult on aircraft, payloads and workflow.

If you run surveys or exploration programmes and this problem sounds familiar, we would like to hear how you handle it today. Request early access at https://aersynk.io

posts.title: Reel: from flight to finished map
posts.instagram:
How does a drone survey become a map?

1. Plan: mark out the area to survey.
2. Fly: the drone flies parallel lines, taking overlapping photos.
3. Process: software matches the photos and builds an orthomosaic (a map you can measure on) and an elevation model of the ground.

That is photogrammetry. The overlap between photos is what lets the software work out the shape of the ground.

Planning a mapping job? Send us a message or visit aersynk.io.

Animated illustration, not real survey data. Voice-over is computer-generated.

posts.title: What is GSD?
alt: What is GSD? Ground sampling distance is the size of one image pixel on the ground. Illustration: a low drone covers a small area with a fine pixel grid; a high drone covers a larger area with a coarse grid.
posts.instagram:
What is GSD?

Ground sampling distance is the size of one image pixel on the ground. It is the number that shapes a whole drone survey.

Fly lower: smaller pixels and more detail, but more flight lines and processing time.
Fly higher: bigger pixels and faster coverage, but less detail.

The right GSD depends on the decision you need to make. Checking cracks on a structure needs far finer detail than a site overview.

Save this for your next survey brief. Questions? Send us a message.
